div.head: IV As 6.3
div.ab: Si autem fugiat (aufugiat), prosequatur eum omnis homo super uitam suam qui uelit quod rex, et occidat eum cui obuiabit. Qui ei pepercerit uel eundem firmauerit, indignus sit omnium que habebit et uite sue, sicut fur, nisi se possit allegiare, quod nec furtum cum eo sciret nec facnum, pro quo uite sue (mortis) reus esset.

Si autem fugiat prosequatur eum omnis homo super vitam suam qui velit quod rex, et occidat eum cui obviabit. Qui ei pepercerit vel eundem firmaverit, indignus sit omnium quæ habebit et vitæ suæ, sicut fur, nisi se possit allegiare quod nec furtum cum eo sciret nec facnum, pro quo vitæ suæ reus esset.

If however he takes to flight, he shall be pursued to his death by all men who are willing to carry out the king's wishes, and whosoever shall meet him shall kill him. And he who spares or harbours him shall forfeit his life and all that he has as if he were a thief himself, unless he can prove that he was not aware of any theft or crime for which his [the fugitive's] life was forfeit.
div.note: Latin only; no German translation in Liebermann. Old English of the last part in H (row 852).
